title: FluidMCP HTTP response isolation — starter example for PR #913

summary.headline: Give each upstream HTTP request a unique ID, validate the response ID, and restore the caller's original ID.
what: Keep caller IDs separate from upstream correlation IDs.
Reject mismatched upstream responses before restoring the original ID.
Exercise delayed echoes through both gateway endpoints under concurrent load.
summary.why: Different callers can send the same JSON-RPC ID; the shared upstream must still distinguish their requests.

impact.label: Transport scope
impact.text: This change and load suite cover Streamable HTTP; stdio and SSE transport clients are outside this example.

flows.title: Request ID round trip
flows.description: The proxy keeps correlation state local to the HTTP invocation. The response must match that invocation's upstream ID before it is relabeled for the caller.

messages.label: Same tool arguments, fresh upstream ID
Result or error with upstream ID
Check upstream ID before restoring original ID

symbols.name: _proxy_to_http_server
symbols.summary: Forward JSON-RPC over HTTP and validate response correlation before restoring the original ID.

symbols.name: run_load
symbols.summary: Compare concurrent caller markers with returned echoes and independent upstream execution records.

review.verdict: Illustrative starter, not a completed review. Expand against the target PR and record actual validation results.

tests.what: Defined scenarios cover 50/100 callers, raw JSON-RPC unique/reused IDs, and convenience tool calls; no execution is claimed by this example.

untested: This example does not establish runtime test results, stdio coverage, SSE transport coverage, or secure-mode authorization.
